newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Arafat start talks in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat start talks in Gaza.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat began talks at the Israel-Gaza border on Sunday on implementing further peace steps agreed in their Hebron deal, officials said.

Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said Arafat wanted to discuss Israel's withdrawal of troops from West Bank rural areas planned for early March, the operation of Palestinian sea and air ports and preparations for crucial "final-status" talks.

The meeting is a followup to last month's accord that handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule and reaffirmed an Israel-PLO commitment to previous peace deals that call for a three-stage Israeli pullback from West Bank rural areas.
The summit had been scheduled for last Thursday but was postponed at Netanyahu's request after 73 Israeli soldiers died in the collision of two Lebanon-bound helicopters on Tuesday.
Netanyahu's aide David Bar-Ilan told Reuters on Saturday night that all the "nitty-gritty" issues in the accord would be discussed as well as Israeli demands that the PLO respect its commitments.

Israel was due to free 25 Palestinian women prisoners on Monday or Tuesday, officials for both sides said. Palestinian sources said they were the total of women prisoners among the 5,000 Palestinians held by Israel.
